subject: Dedicated demo - Nimbus Analytics (throughput & latency reqs)
messages:
From: Rahul Singh <rahul@nimbus.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity for low-latency inference

Hi Marissa,

We signed up for a trial of Redwood yesterday and the app is looking promising. Our production workload requires sustained throughput (~500 concurrent streams) and P95 latency under 200ms for short-form generation (<=256 tokens). We selected the Dedicated capacity option in the portal and the form asked to schedule a demo / technical sync.

Can we schedule a 45-minute session next week where we can walk through Dedicated capacity, autoscaling/burst behavior, and performance testing? We'll have our infra lead (Priya) and a couple of ML engineers on the call.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our traffic profile and a couple of sample prompts.

Thanks,
Rahul Singh
Head of ML Ops
Nimbus Analytics

Attachment: nimbus-performance-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)

I'm available next Tue/Wed afternoon PST. Would 11/19 at 10:00am PST or 11/20 at 11:00am PST work for you and Priya?

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Hi Priya / Rahul  looking forward to the call tomorrow. Quick notes so we can make the most of the 45 min:

- I'll cover workload sizing: how we translate concurrency + tokens/sec into GPU pool sizing and the assumptions for batching.
- I'll show measured P95 numbers from a comparable customer (similar prompt lengths) and the trade-offs when enabling larger batch sizes or KV cache.
- We'll demo autoscaling/burst and expected cold-start windows for new sessions.

A couple of questions  could you confirm:
1) Typical average prompt length (tokens) and distribution (you sent sample prompts but we need confirmation)
2) Whether you have any hard latency SLOs (e.g., P95 < 200ms) vs. best-effort targets

If you can drop those answers into the shared spreadsheet before the meeting, we can tailor the test plan.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
